Updated assessment incorporating the Beige Book:
- The FOMC statement is clearly hawkish (75 bp hike to 3–3.25%, guidance of “ongoing increases,” and continued balance-sheet reduction), keeping policy firmly in restrictive territory amid elevated inflation.
- The August 2022 Beige Book points to flat-to-modest economic activity overall, with New York noting higher recession risk even as tourism remains solid and employment continues to rise. Several districts reported easing in some input costs (steel, lumber, copper), but price pressures remain broad.
- Beige Book- and survey-backed credit dynamics: banks reported tighter standards and terms across C&I and CRE, as well as tighter household credit (credit cards, subprime auto, jumbo/GSE mortgages, HELOCs). Demand was mixed—stronger for some business credit and HELOCs, weaker across several CRE categories.
- Taken together, the Beige Book and SLOOS suggest bank credit supply is tightening and will amplify the FOMC’s restrictive stance, heightening downside risks to growth, capex, and CRE even as headline inflation may gradually benefit from some easing input costs.

Net: tilt the sentiment more negative than a policy-statement-only read given slowing activity and tighter credit conditions.
